definitions.rationale: Concrete recursive equation defining factRun for the I <= N step; it advances the index and multiplies the accumulator without matching operational configuration cells.
definitions.text:
rule factRun(I, N, F) => factRun(I +Int 1, N, F *Int I)
    requires I <=Int N
    [concrete]

definitions.rationale: Concrete base equation defining factRun when I > N by returning the accumulated product.
definitions.text:
rule factRun(I, N, F) => F
    requires I >Int N
    [concrete]

definitions.rationale: Simplification-form duplicate of the factRun base equation under the same I > N guard, so it is definitional normalization rather than an additional fact.
definitions.text:
rule factRun(I, N, F) => F
    requires I >Int N
    [simplification]

definitions.rationale: Concrete recursive equation defining totalRun for the I <= N step by advancing the index and adding I to the accumulator.
definitions.text:
rule totalRun(I, N, T) => totalRun(I +Int 1, N, T +Int I)
    requires I <=Int N
    [concrete]

definitions.rationale: Concrete base equation defining totalRun when I > N by returning the accumulated sum.
definitions.text:
rule totalRun(I, N, T) => T
    requires I >Int N
    [concrete]

definitions.rationale: Simplification-form duplicate of the totalRun base equation under the identical I > N guard.
definitions.text:
rule totalRun(I, N, T) => T
    requires I >Int N
    [simplification]

definitions.rationale: Concrete even-index recurrence defining resultRun by appending F*I and advancing all three loop accumulators.
definitions.text:
rule resultRun(VS, I, N, F, T)
    => resultRun(
         valSeqConcat(VS, vCons(F *Int I, .ValSeq)),
         I +Int 1,
         N,
         F *Int I,
         T +Int I)
    requires I <=Int N andBool pyMod(I, 2) ==Int 0
    [concrete]

definitions.rationale: Concrete odd-index recurrence defining resultRun by appending T+I and advancing the index, product, and sum accumulators.
definitions.text:
rule resultRun(VS, I, N, F, T)
    => resultRun(
         valSeqConcat(
           VS,
           vCons(T +Int I, .ValSeq)),
         I +Int 1,
         N,
         F *Int I,
         T +Int I)
    requires I <=Int N andBool pyMod(I, 2) =/=Int 0
    [concrete]

definitions.rationale: Concrete base equation defining resultRun when I > N by returning the accumulated value sequence.
definitions.text:
rule resultRun(VS, I, N, _F, _T) => VS
    requires I >Int N
    [concrete]

definitions.rationale: Simplification-form duplicate of the resultRun base equation under the same I > N guard.
definitions.text:
rule resultRun(VS, I, N, _F, _T) => VS
    requires I >Int N
    [simplification]

source_rules.rationale: Reverse-step equality used to fold factRun during symbolic proof; Stage 1 does not first prove this exact rule in a module that omits it, so it is an additional trusted mathematical fact rather than a proved derived lemma.
source_rules.text:
rule factRun(I +Int 1, N, F *Int I) => factRun(I, N, F)
    requires I <=Int N
    [simplification]

source_rules.rationale: Reverse-step equality used to fold totalRun during symbolic proof; it is present in the compiled proof definition and has no prior exact proof against a module without the rule.
source_rules.text:
rule totalRun(I +Int 1, N, T +Int I) => totalRun(I, N, T)
    requires I <=Int N
    [simplification]

source_rules.rationale: Even-case reverse-step equality that folds an advanced resultRun term; Stage 1 assumes it in verification.k before proving the targets and supplies no earlier exact proof without it.
source_rules.text:
rule resultRun(
         valSeqConcat(VS, vCons(F *Int I, .ValSeq)),
         I +Int 1,
         N,
         F *Int I,
         T +Int I)
    => resultRun(VS, I, N, F, T)
    requires I <=Int N andBool pyMod(I, 2) ==Int 0
    [simplification]

source_rules.rationale: Odd-case reverse-step equality that folds an advanced resultRun term; it is a proof-closing mathematical fact not separately established by the mounted Stage 1 proof.
source_rules.text:
rule resultRun(
         valSeqConcat(VS, vCons(T +Int I, .ValSeq)),
         I +Int 1,
         N,
         F *Int I,
         T +Int I)
    => resultRun(VS, I, N, F, T)
    requires I <=Int N andBool pyMod(I, 2) =/=Int 0
    [simplification]
